title: 2026 U.S. Senate election in New Hampshire
description: Open 2026 U.S. Senate race in New Hampshire for the seat held by retiring Sen. Jeanne Shaheen. The contest is drawing attention because New Hampshire is a competitive statewide battleground, with Democrats and Republicans testing different paths to the seat through the general election and the Sept. 8 primary.

candidates.name: Chris Pappas
candidates.summary: Chris Pappas is the Democratic U.S. representative for New Hampshire's 1st Congressional District and a candidate for the open Senate seat in 2026. In April 2026, his campaign highlighted a child care cost plan as part of its broader tax-and-costs message.

summary_sources.title: Chris Pappas for Senate Highlights Plan to Lower Child Care Costs for Granite State Families

Healthcare.stance: Chris Pappas supports extending and restoring ACA premium tax credits, and backing a public option with stronger accountability for insurers and drugmakers to lower costs. He also backs capping insulin at $35 per month, enabling Medicare to negotiate drug prices, expanding telehealth, and opposing Medicaid cuts.

Economy.stance: Pappas says he is focused on lowering costs for working families and small businesses, including food, energy, and drug costs. His campaign also says he supports cracking down on corporate and AI-driven price gouging and protecting nutrition assistance.

Abortion & Reproductive Health.stance: Chris Pappas supports codifying abortion rights and safeguarding access to reproductive health care. He backed the Women’s Health Protection Act and introduced or supported measures to reaffirm the right to travel across state lines for abortion care and to protect access to IVF, and has advocated for maintaining funding for Planned Parenthood health centers.

Immigration.stance: Pappas has called for congressional oversight of ICE and for preserving local control over immigration-related decisions. He has also said some ICE funding should be redirected to local law enforcement.

He supports expanding Pell Grants, making community college and public universities tuition-free, increasing protections for student borrowers, funding career training and apprenticeships, restoring federal education funds to New Hampshire, and expanding VA education benefits for in‑demand fields, while safeguarding public education from federal cuts.

candidates.summary: Scott Brown is a former U.S. senator from Massachusetts and the Republican nominee in New Hampshire's 2014 Senate race. In the 2026 cycle, he is running for the open New Hampshire Senate seat and was trailing John E. Sununu in the Republican primary polling cited in January 2026.

Foreign Policy.stance: Brown states that Iran has destabilized the Middle East and supports taking targeted military action against Iran's nuclear facilities when necessary, while arguing that prolonged wars should require a formal declaration of war by Congress rather than open-ended engagement.

Economy.stance: Brown emphasizes affordability as the core of his economic agenda for New Hampshire, calling for lower energy costs and housing costs through expanded energy supply (notably natural gas access and nuclear energy at Seabrook) and streamlined housing development via regulatory reform and public-private partnerships; he frames policy as bipartisan and state-local-federal coordination to relieve the cost of living for working families.

Climate/Energy.stance: Scott Brown has emphasized making energy affordable for Granite Staters, focusing on reducing energy costs and opposing rate increases, while supporting a pro‑growth energy policy that includes domestic energy production and streamlined permitting to lower prices.

Tech & AI.stance: Scott Brown supports serious federal guardrails on AI to protect workers from displacement and emphasizes expanding community college and trade-school training to prepare Americans for AI-enabled energy and infrastructure jobs; he rejects a 'Wild West' approach to AI.

Firearms & Second Amendment.stance: Based on recent reporting, Scott Brown has engaged with gun-rights groups and has shown interest in campus carry policy discussions in New Hampshire. While earlier coverage suggested he supported federal gun restrictions at times, his 2026 campaign appearances include meetings with gun-rights supporters, indicating a focus on Second Amendment rights and nuanced gun-safety policy rather than sweeping changes; no comprehensive statewide platform has been published as of now.

Education.stance: Brown supports making early education and child care more affordable by leveraging existing federal and state resources and advancing a collaborative approach among local, state, and federal governments and families to address childcare challenges.

candidates.name: John E. Sununu
candidates.summary: John E. Sununu is a former Republican U.S. senator from New Hampshire who previously served in the U.S. House and is running again for the Senate in 2026. He is part of New Hampshire's Sununu political family and is campaigning on a message centered on affordability, fiscal restraint, and independent leadership.

candidates.name: Karishma Manzur
candidates.summary: Karishma Manzur is a scientist and Democratic candidate in the 2026 New Hampshire Senate race. In the January 2026 UNH Survey Center poll, she trailed Chris Pappas by a wide margin in the Democratic primary testing.

summary_sources.title: Sununu, Pappas Frontrunners in 2026 NH Senate Race; Ayotte Favored for Re-Election as Governor

Economy.stance: Karishma Manzur advocates for a bottom-up, pro-worker economy that raises wages, strengthens unions, and reduces the influence of money in politics. Her economic plan includes passing the PRO Act, raising the federal minimum wage to a living wage, expanding job training and apprenticeships, and overturning Citizens United to restore campaign finance transparency.

sources.title: Our Priorities - Karishma for Senate

Foreign Policy.stance: Karishma Manzur advocates a diplomacy-first, restraint-based foreign policy that ends 'blank checks' for war and increases congressional oversight of military action. She supports reducing U.S. involvement in overseas conflicts and prioritizing diplomacy, human rights, and peaceful, lawful solutions over broad military spending.

sources.title: Peace Action Endorses Karishma Manzur for U.S. Senate
Manzur running for Senate to serve constituents, not donors
Our Priorities

Civil Rights & Equality.stance: Civil Rights & Equality: Karishma Manzur positions civil rights and equality as central to her policy agenda, emphasizing defending constitutional rights, expanding democratic participation, and opposing discriminatory practices; she advocates for reducing the influence of money in politics to ensure government serves all Granite Staters.

sources.title: Karishma Manzur for Senate – Official Campaign Website

Education.stance: Karishma Manzur advocates for universal, high-quality public education funded by federal and state partners—from pre-K through K-12, community colleges, and public universities—along with universal childcare to support families. She supports expanding apprenticeships and job-training, maintaining inclusive education policies, expanding the Child Tax Credit, and opposing federal school voucher programs.

sources.title: Karishma Manzur launches education platform
Our Priorities - Karishma for Senate
As New Hampshire's US Senate race ramps up, candidates outline positions on improving child care

Election Policy.stance: Karishma Manzur supports sweeping democracy reform to curb money in politics, including overturning Citizens United, banning corporate PACs, dark money, and super PACs, and restoring public financing for campaigns. She also advocates stronger ethics rules, including banning stock trading by Members of Congress and a five-year cooling-off period before lobbying.

Local Issues.stance: Karishma Manzur will tackle New Hampshire's local affordability crisis by expanding federal housing funding (HUD/Section 8), promoting union-built, energy-efficient housing, and restricting private equity in housing to stabilize rents. She also supports universal, affordable child care by expanding federal subsidies so families pay no more than 7% of income on care, and strengthening the Child Tax Credit to reduce the cost of living.

sources.title: Our Priorities - Karishma for Senate

candidates.name: Jared Sullivan
candidates.summary: Jared Sullivan is a Democratic member of the New Hampshire House of Representatives from the Grafton 2 district and is running for U.S. Senate in 2026. He has said his campaign is focused on restoring trust in government, addressing housing affordability, and pushing for democratic reforms such as campaign finance changes and ranked-choice voting.

Climate/Energy.stance: Sullivan’s campaign site lists environment as a priority, but the public material reviewed here does not provide a detailed energy platform. Based on available sources, his public position is that environmental policy is part of his campaign agenda, but specific proposals on energy production, regulation, or climate targets were not clearly stated.

sources.title: Jared for NH

Immigration.stance: Sullivan says immigration enforcement should include accountability and due-process protections, and he has said ICE abuses have eroded trust in the agency. He supports comprehensive immigration reform and has said simply abolishing an agency without reform does not solve the underlying problems.

sources.title: The Dartmouth
Laconia Daily Sun

Civil Rights & Equality.stance: Sullivan ties civil-rights concerns to due-process protections, especially in immigration enforcement, and says government should respect constitutional rights. He also supports democratic reforms such as ranked-choice voting and open primaries to make government more representative.

sources.title: The Dartmouth
Laconia Daily Sun

Election Policy.stance: Sullivan supports campaign finance reform, independent redistricting, ranked-choice voting, and open primaries. He has said he wants to reduce the influence of money in politics and overturn Citizens United.

reviews.summary: This is a well-researched, balanced profile of the 2026 New Hampshire Senate race with strong sourcing across six candidates. The polling data is clearly attributed to three reputable NH polling organizations (UNH, Saint Anselm, Emerson) with sample sizes and dates. Candidate backgrounds, issue positions, and endorsements are sourced primarily from official campaign sites, credible news outlets (WMUR, The Dartmouth, NH Public Radio, CNN), government records (House.gov, FEC, Congressional voting records), and established issue-tracking platforms (Citizens Count, Vote Smart, OpenSecrets). The profile demonstrates a good-faith search effort for all candidates, including lower-profile Republican primary contenders. Language is neutral and nonpartisan across all candidate profiles. Where information is unavailable (e.g., some candidates' education/career history, Sununu's detailed climate platform), the profile transparently marks confidence as 'low' rather than making unsupported inferences. One minor internal inconsistency note applies (see flags).

flags.concern: The stance is described with low confidence and acknowledges conflicting historical and current reporting; while this is an accurate reflection of the search results, it highlights a lack of a clear, consolidated platform from the candidate.
The source cited for Israel & Gaza refers to the campaign website, but the stance itself is not explicitly articulated in the summary provided.
flags.suggestion: Update the stance text to reflect the campaign's specific messaging on the Middle East, or maintain as 'no detailed position found' if the site does not contain concrete policy points.

flags.concern: The stance text is a placeholder: 'To be updated based on new sources'.
flags.suggestion: Replace this placeholder with a summary of the candidate's actual public statements on immigration or change the stance to 'No public position found' if none are available.

Polling data from reputable pollsters (UNH, Saint Anselm, Emerson) is accurately aggregated and cited to primary URLs. Chris Pappas section stands out with detailed career history, voting records (e.g., H.R. 82 from House Clerk), top donors (OpenSecrets), and high-confidence issue stances backed by 10+ campaign/government sources per topic. Other candidates' issues appropriately note 'no public position found' with search evidence (e.g., Citizens Count for minor candidates), avoiding fabrication. Language remains neutral and factual throughout.
